earlier_scan.source_named: Edmondson, J.A. 2003. Three Tibeto-Burman Languages of Vietnam; Lama 2012 UTA diss. (Mantsi described as 6-tone; no stress statement read)

sources.citation: Iwasa, Kazue et al. 2017. Tone and accent in Tibeto-Burman. In Endo, M. (ed.), Studies in Asian Geolinguistics VII: Tone and Accent, pp.12ff. Tokyo: ILCAA.https://publication.aa-ken.jp/sag7_tone_2017.pdf
sources.note: Typological survey: Lolo-Burmese languages classed 'A-1 Syllable tone'; Mantsi is not named individually. Generic/second-hand only.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages: a study from the perspectives of shared innovation and phylogenetic estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. hdl:10106/11161.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: p.84 sketch: 'Mondzi [mo21ndʑi21] is spoken in Funing County, Yunnan and in Hà Giang province, Vietnam.. Mondzi has 40 initials, 27 vowels.., 6 tones (/55/, /44/, /33/, /53/, /13/, and /21/) (cf. YYFC 1983).' The word 'stress' does not occur in the dissertation. Lama's Mondzi data are the Funing (China) variety = Glottolog mond1267, sister of mant1265.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. n.d. [2017-]. MSEA Languages website: 'Mondzish branch' and 'Munji' field-notes pages.https://sites.google.com/site/msealangs/mondzish-branch
sources.note: Classification and wordlist-recording notes (Munji of Malipo); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. In Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14), 62-81. Taipei: Academia Sinica (+ presentation slides). Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1127814.
sources.note: Classification and comparative lexicon; sec. 2.6 'Munji and Mantsi' is distributional/lexical. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2013. New endangered Tibeto-Burman languages of southwestern China: Mondzish, Longjia, Pherbu, and others. Presentation slides. Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1127796.

sources.note: Sec. 5 'Lolo' (pp.314-316) on Red Lolo [ma53 tsi53] of Meo Vac (speaker La Thi Mi): initial inventory, rhymes, and 'Red Lolo [ma53 tsi53] has five tones with values 53, 31, 312, 44, and 35, which we have not plotted here.' Nothing on stress/accent anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence: no hits).

sources.note: Title/record only. A 10-page Vietnamese description of 'the Lô Lô language in Hà Giang' in the Institute of Linguistics journal; sketches of this genre normally give the syllable structure and the number of thanh điệu (tones) with pitch values and examples, which would make it the earliest modern first-hand tone count for Mantsi (cf. Edmondson 2003: five tones 53, 31, 312, 44, 35 for Red Lolo of Mèo Vạc). Glottolog types it 'minimal'.
